newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: INTERVIEW - Hyundai Motor sees R&D as key to future.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Hyundai Motor sees R&D as key to future.

text.p: Stymied by stagnant sales at home, South Korea's largest carmaker Hyundai Motor Co sees research and development as the path to future profits, the company president said on Thursday.
"Our policy priority will be on technological development. This is essential to satisfying out customers," Park Byung-jae told Reuters in an interview.
Hyundai's R&D investment would be raised to seven percent of total sales this year, from 5.5 percent in 1996, he said.
"About 900 billion won will be spent in research activities this year and the investment portion will be maintained at seven percent in the future," Park said.
Further, he said the percentage of the company's workforce devoted to R&D activities would be increased to 20 percent in 2000 from the current 13 percent.

"Economic recovery, a strong yen and other external factors will help us to recover. But more importantly, our long-term strategy on how to improve our international competitiveness will decide our future," said Park, pausing frequently to collect his thoughts.
For this year, Park said Hyundai's sales sould be 13 trillion won ($14.64 billion), lower than the company's earlier target of 13.5 trillion, because of sluggish domestic sales.
Sales of Hyundai Motor, a flagship unit of the Hyundai Group HYGR.CN, totalled 11.49 trillion won in 1996.
"Domestic sales this year are expected to remain at last year's level. The overall economic slowdown is mainly to blame," Park said.
He said domestic sales would fall to 750,000 units this year, down from its target of 825,000 units. Hyundai's sales at home last year were 740,000 units.
However, he said the company could meet its export target of 675,000 units this year, which is higher than last year's exports of 570,000.
"Our mid-sized sedans and Tiburon sport cars sell well overseas. So I think there will be no problems in meeting the export target," Park said.
Analysts said Hyundai's emphasis on technology was the right move.

"Hyundai has been very prudent in investment decisions. Its policies are sharply focused on technological improvement. The company deserves to be the country's largest and best carmaker," said Yang Dong-ki, analyst at Dongbang Peregrine Securities.
Park said Hyundai's annual production capacity would rise to 2.4 million units by 2000 from the current 1.65 milllion.
"Our production will rise largely in other nations from now on. India, China, Europe and Russia are regions that we think are very important for our expansion projects," Park said.
He said a joint venture plant in Turkey would begin producing sub-compact cars and vans from July at an annual rate of 50,000 units.
"The capacity will soon rise to 100,000 units," he said.

Hyundai also is expected to complete a plant in India with an annual capacity of 200,000 cars by the end of 1998. Hyundai officials said the $1.1 billion India project would be entirely invested by Hyundai.
Hyundai is scheduled to complete a joint venture plant in Indonesia capable of churning out 100,000 units a year by 1999.
"In addition, we are negotiating with China to build a finishied car plant," Park said. ($1 = 887.70 won)
